summary.headline: Orders and revenue both beat target in week of 06 Apr; revenue up 11.6% week on week, but the year to date stays behind target.

points.what: Orders reached 889, up 4.5% week on week and 71.6% year on year, above the 8-week range.
points.so_what: Orders came in 35 above the weekly target of 854, an attainment of 104.1%.

points.what: Gross revenue was $67,572, up 11.6% week on week and 90.5% year on year.
points.so_what: That is $9,614 above the weekly revenue target and ahead of the 75% growth the targets assume.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue of $128,119 is 108.3% of the $118,256 target for these two weeks.
points.so_what: The quarter is ahead early, with $755,967 still needed over the remaining 11 weeks to reach the full-quarter target of $884,086.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 23 Mar 2026 was 11.5%, up 2.2 pp week on week, assessed as bad.
points.so_what: This is the most recent week with full 14-day history, so it is the current read on return behaviour.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 23 Mar 2026 rose 2.2 pp to 11.5% and sits 3.1 pp above last year, both assessed as bad.
points.so_what: The rise clears the 1.0 pp notable threshold, so return behaviour is worth tracking as later weeks mature.

points.what: Return rates for the two most recent weeks are not yet reported, as those orders have not completed the full 14 days.
points.so_what: Return behaviour for the reporting week cannot be judged yet and will only be visible in about two weeks.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue of $843,676 is 94.5% of the $892,811 target to date, a gap of $49,135.
points.so_what: Reaching the $3,888,802 full-year target requires $80,135 per week, against a recent 8-week run-rate of $60,216.

points.what: Weekly orders hit 104.1% of target and weekly revenue 116.6%, both ahead.
points.so_what: Next week's targets step up to 892 orders and $66,235 of revenue.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue is 108.3% of target, $9,863 ahead after two weeks of 13.
points.so_what: $755,967 of the $884,086 full-quarter target still remains across the final 11 weeks.

points.what: Year to date is behind at 94.5% of target, with Jan, Feb and Mar all below target and only Apr month-to-date ahead.
points.so_what: The required $80,135 weekly run-rate for the remaining 38 weeks sits well above the current 8-week run-rate of $60,216.

points.what: LATAM orders rose 36.9% to 152, contributing 41 of the 38-order weekly increase, or 107.9% of the change.
points.so_what: LATAM accounts for more than the entire weekly gain, offsetting declines elsewhere.

points.what: APAC orders fell 0.8% to 372 and North America fell 4.0% to 194, together contributing minus 11 orders.
points.so_what: The two largest regions, at 41.8% and 21.8% of orders, held back the week's total.

points.what: Facebook and Display each added 15 orders, 39.5% of the change apiece, while Search was flat at 608 orders.
points.so_what: Search still carries 68.4% of all orders, so the week's growth sat with the smaller sources.

points.what: AOV rose 7.9% week on week to $89.50 and is 9.3% above last year, assessed as good.
points.so_what: Revenue grew faster than orders, at 11.6% versus 4.5%, in line with the higher value per order.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose 0.9 pp to 15.1%, assessed as bad, though it remains 1.3 pp below last year.
points.so_what: Each percentage point of cancellation is worth about $796 of weekly revenue.

points.what: New customer signups were 251, down 3.1% week on week and 3.1% year on year, both assessed as bad.
points.so_what: Signups are falling while orders grow 71.6% year on year, so the week's volume leans on existing customers.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 23 Mar 2026 was 11.5%, versus 8.4% a year earlier.
points.so_what: Returns are not deducted from gross revenue, so order quality is weaker than the revenue figure alone suggests.

summary.headline: Strong week: orders and revenue both above target and above their 8-week range, but the year to date remains behind target.

points.what: Orders reached 889, up 4.5% on the prior week and up 71.6% year on year, outside the 8-week range.
points.so_what: This is a notable step up from the 8-week average of 803 orders and lifts the week to 104.1% of its order target.

points.what: Gross revenue was $67,572, up 11.6% week on week and up 90.5% year on year, reaching 116.6% of the weekly target.
points.so_what: Revenue growth of 90.5% is running ahead of the 75% growth the targets assume for the year.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue of $128,119 is 108.3% of target, while year-to-date revenue of $843,676 is 94.5% of target.
points.so_what: A strong quarter start has not yet closed the $49,135 year-to-date shortfall built up in January, February and March.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 23 Mar 2026 rose to 11.5%, up 2.2 pp on the week before.
points.so_what: This is assessed as bad and is the main quality concern behind an otherwise positive week.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 23 Mar 2026 was 11.5%, up 2.2 pp week on week and up 3.1 pp year on year.
points.so_what: Both movements are assessed as bad and the increase is above the 1.0 pp notable threshold.

points.what: The return rate is reported for the week of 23 Mar 2026 because the two most recent weeks are not yet mature.
points.so_what: Returns for the reporting week cannot be judged yet, so this figure should not be read as covering 6 to 12 Apr.

points.what: New customer signups were 251, down 3.1% week on week and down 3.1% year on year.
points.so_what: Both movements are assessed as bad, in contrast to orders growing 71.6% year on year.

points.what: The week delivered 889 orders against a target of 854 (104.1%) and $67,572 revenue against $57,958 (116.6%), both ahead.
points.so_what: Next week's targets step up to 892 orders and $66,235 of revenue.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue is $128,119 versus $118,256 of target, 108.3% and $9,863 ahead after 2 of 13 weeks.
points.so_what: $755,967 of the $884,086 full-quarter target still has to be earned across the remaining 11 weeks.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue is $843,676 against $892,811 of target, 94.5% and $49,135 behind, with 38 weeks left.
points.so_what: Hitting the $3,888,802 full-year target needs $80,135 a week, well above the recent 8-week run-rate of $60,216.

points.what: LATAM added 41 orders, up 36.9% to 152, accounting for 107.9% of the total weekly order change.
points.so_what: LATAM alone more than covers the week's net gain of 38 orders, making it the single driver of growth.

points.what: APAC fell 3 orders to 372 and North America fell 8 orders to 194, while EMEA added 8 orders to 171.
points.so_what: The two largest regions did not contribute to growth this week, even though all four regions are up year on year.

points.what: By traffic source, Facebook and Display each added 15 orders, 39.5% of the change each, while Search was flat at 608 orders.
points.so_what: The week's gain came from the smaller sources, with Search, at 68.4% of orders, holding its level.

points.what: Average order value rose 7.9% week on week to $89.50 and is 9.3% above the same week last year.
points.so_what: Higher value per order explains why revenue grew 11.6% while orders grew 4.5%.

points.what: The order cancellation rate was 15.1%, up 0.9 pp on the prior week but 1.3 pp below the same week last year.
points.so_what: Each percentage point of cancellations is worth about $796 of revenue at this week's volumes.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 23 Mar 2026 was 11.5%, against 8.4% a year earlier.
points.so_what: Order quality on returns is weaker than last year, unlike the cancellation rate, which improved year on year.

points.what: New signups of 251 were down 3.1% week on week and year on year, while orders were up 71.6% year on year.
points.so_what: Order growth is not currently being matched by growth in the new customer base.
